This matter was called on for hearing today.

Coram :
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice J.B. Pardiwala

For Petitioner(s) :
 Mr. Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, Adv.

 Mr. Anil Kumar Sinha, Adv.
 Mrs. Rachna Gupta, AOR  UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.
Exemption Applications are allowed.

2. The petitioners have been denied anticipatory bail by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad in connection with FIR No.27/24 lodged at Kotwali Katra Police Station, District Mirzapur, U.P. for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 304B of the Indian Penal Code (for short, `IPC)
and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act respectively.

sentences.text: It is the case of the prosecution that the deceased committed suicide due to harassment caused by the accused persons named in the First Information Report for demand of dowry.

5. Heard Mr. Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Mr. Anil Kumar Sinha, the learned counsel appearing for the State of U.P.
6.

It appears that while the anticipatory bail application of the petitioners  herein was pending before the High Court, they were granted protection on the condition that they shall cooperate with the investigation and appear before the Trial Court.
However, the petitioners are stated to have not cooperated with the investigation and also failed to appear before the Trial Court.
7. In such circumstances, referred to above, the petitioners are hear before this Court with the present petition.
8. We are informed that the in-laws at the time of the unfortunate incident were residing separately and that too at their native village.
The deceased was residing at her matrimonial home along with her husband.
We are further informed that the husband has already been enlarged on regular bail.
9. It appears that the investigation has been completed and charge-sheet has also been filed against the petitioners.

10. In such circumstances, referred to above, we direct the petitioners now to appear before the Trial Court and furnish bail to the satisfaction of the Trial Court and further subject to the terms and conditions that the Trial Court may deem fit to impose.
11. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands disposed of.
12. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
(VISHAL ANAND) (POOJA SHARMA)
